Question: To what extent are students’ family socioeconomic status, parental education, and home learning resources associated with their mathematics performance in PISA 2025?

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r load-lib, message = FALSE}
# Add any other libraries here
library(tidyverse)
library(learningtower)
library(haven)
library(ggplot2)

```

```{r load-data}
# load your data 
student_math <- read_rds("data/student_math.rds")
```

```{r detect and remove missing value}
# summary(mean, median, max, NAs)
student_math |>
  summary()
# Remove unnecessary columns and missing math scores
student_math_pro <- student_math |>
  select(-general_family_support) |>
  filter(
    if_all(
      starts_with("math_score_pv"),
      ~ !is.na(.)
    )
  )

```

```{r select researching dataset}
# Select variables for data processing

student_processed <- student_math_pro |>
  select(
    student_id,
    country_code,
    student_age,
    student_gender,
    family_socioeconomic_status,
    family_support,
    home_possessions_index,
    home_ict_resources,
    highest_parental_education,
    parental_education_years,
    highest_parental_occupational_status,
    starts_with("math_score_pv")
  )
# calculate mean score for each student
student_processed <- student_processed |>
  mutate(
    math_score = rowMeans(
      across(starts_with("math_score_pv"))
    )
  ) |>
  select(-starts_with("math_score_pv"))
# Calculate statistics
score_stats <- student_processed %>%
  filter(!is.na(math_score)) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_score = mean(math_score),
    median_score = median(math_score),
    q1 = quantile(math_score, 0.25),
    q3 = quantile(math_score, 0.75)
  )

```

```{r Tidy Data}
# Variable Table
variable_table <- tibble(
  Variable = names(student_processed)
) |>
  mutate(
    Category = case_when(
      Variable %in% c(
        "student_id",
        "country_code",
        "student_age",
        "student_gender"
      ) ~ "Student Information",

      Variable %in% c(
        "family_socioeconomic_status",
        "highest_parental_occupational_status"
      ) ~ "Family SES",

      Variable %in% c(
        "highest_parental_education",
        "parental_education_years"
      ) ~ "Parental Education",

      Variable %in% c(
        "family_support",
        "home_possessions_index",
        "home_ict_resources"
      ) ~ "Home Learning Environment",

      Variable == "math_score" ~ "Mathematics Performance"
    )
  ) |>
  select(Category, Variable)
variable_table

```

```{r Visualising overall}

# Calculate the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles
ci <- quantile(
  student_processed$math_score,
  probs = c(0.025, 0.975)
)

ggplot(student_processed, aes(x = math_score)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 50,
    fill = "steelblue",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  geom_vline(
    xintercept = ci,
    color = "#D98282",
    linetype = "dashed",
    linewidth = 1
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = ci[1],
    y = Inf,
    label = paste0("2.5%: ", round(ci[1], 2)),
    color = "#D98282",
    vjust = 1.5,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = ci[2],
    y = Inf,
    label = paste0("97.5%: ", round(ci[2], 2)),
    color = "#D98282",
    vjust = 1.5,
    size = 3.5
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Mathematics Scores",
    subtitle = "Central 95% of Mathematics Scores | PISA 2025",
    x = "Mathematics Score",
    y = "Number of Students"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r parental education}
#the relationship between parental education years and mathematics score
# Prepare data
education_data <- student_processed %>%
  filter(
    as.numeric(highest_parental_education) %in% 1:9,
    !is.na(math_score)
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    parental_education = factor(
      as.numeric(highest_parental_education),
      levels = 1:9,
      labels = c(
        "No Qualification",
        "Lower Secondary",
        "Upper Secondary (No Tertiary Access)",
        "Upper Secondary (Tertiary Access)",
        "Post-secondary Non-tertiary",
        "Short-cycle Tertiary",
        "Bachelor's Degree",
        "Master's Degree",
        "Doctoral Degree"
      )
    )
  )


# Violin plot
ggplot(
    education_data,
    aes(
        x = parental_education,
        y = math_score
    )
) +
    geom_violin(
        trim = TRUE,
        fill = "#DCD6F7",
        colour = "#7566A8",
        alpha = 0.8
    ) +
    geom_boxplot(
        width = 0.12,
        outlier.shape = NA,
        fill = "white",
        colour = "#493A70",
        linewidth = 0.5
    ) +
    labs(
        title = "Parental Education and Mathematics Performance",
        subtitle = "PISA 2025 Student Data",
        x = "Highest Parental Education",
        y = "Mathematics Score"
    ) +
    coord_flip() +
    theme_minimal()
```

```{r main2}
#the relationship between highest parental occupational status and mathematics scores
student_processed|>
filter(
    !is.na(highest_parental_occupational_status)
  ) |>
ggplot(
  aes(
    x = highest_parental_occupational_status,
    y = math_score
  )
) +
  geom_hex(bins = 50) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "#EFF6FB",
    high = "#20577F",
    trans = "log10",
    name = "Number of students"
)+
  labs(
    title = "Parental Occupational Status and Mathematics Achievement",
    x = "Family Highest Occupational grade",
    y = "Mathematics score"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r main3}
#the relationship between ICT and mathematics score
clean_data <- student_processed |>
     filter(
         is.finite(home_ict_resources)
     ) 
 ggplot(
    clean_data,
    aes(x = home_ict_resources, y = math_score)
) +
    
    stat_summary_bin(
        fun = mean,
        bins = 1000,
        geom = "point",
        colour = "#F2A6B3",
        size = 1
    ) +
    geom_smooth(
    method = "gam",
    colour = "skyblue",
    linewidth = 1.1
)+
    labs(
        title = "Home ICT Resources and Mathematics score",
        x = "Home ICT Resources Index",
        y = "Mean Mathematics score in each class"
    ) +
    theme_minimal()

```
